meta.promptText: Which vitamin C serum should I buy for dark spots and dull skin in India?

response.text:
For **dark spots + dull skin**, I’d prioritize a **stable 10–15% vitamin C serum** and, most importantly, daily sunscreen.

### My top picks in India

### [Minimalist Vitamin C 10% Face Serum]()
*₹284*

### [Deconstruct Face Serum]()
*₹458*

### [Minimalist 16% Vitamin C + E + Ferulic Acid Face Serum]()
*₹569.10*

### [Plum 15% Vitamin C Face Serum]()
*₹227*

**🥇 Best overall for most people: Minimalist Vitamin C 10% + 1% Acetyl Glucosamine**

It uses **10% Ethyl Ascorbic Acid**, a stable vitamin-C derivative, plus 1% acetyl glucosamine. It's specifically positioned for dullness, uneven tone and dark spots, and is fragrance-free. [beminimalist.co](https://beminimalist.co/products/vitamin-c-ethyl-ascorbic-acid-10-acetyl-glucosamine-1?_pos=5&_sid=5fed91241&_ss=r&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**🥈 Best if you want a gentler formula: Deconstruct 10% Vitamin C + 0.5% Ferulic Acid**

The liposomal vitamin C + ferulic acid combination is appealing if you're new to vitamin C or have somewhat sensitive skin. It also contains centella and panthenol for barrier support. [thedeconstruct.in](https://thedeconstruct.in/products/vitamin-c-and-ferulic-acid-serum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**🥉 Stronger option: Minimalist 16% Vitamin C + E + Ferulic**

I'd choose this if you've already used vitamin C without irritation and want something more potent. Minimalist reports improvements in glow/dullness and spots over several weeks. [beminimalist.co](https://beminimalist.co/collections/daily-dose-of-vitamins-for-skin/products/vitamin-c-e-ferulic-16?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### What I'd buy

If you haven't used vitamin C before, **go with Minimalist 10%**. It's a good balance of effectiveness, stability and price.

Use **2–3 drops in the morning**, followed by moisturizer and **SPF 50 sunscreen**. Start every other morning for the first 1–2 weeks if your skin is sensitive. Don't expect dark spots to disappear in a few days—consistent use generally takes **several weeks to months**, and sunscreen is crucial for preventing pigmentation from coming back. [www.whowhatwear.com](https://www.whowhatwear.com/beauty/skin/best-products-for-hyperpigmentation?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

If you tell me your **skin type (oily/dry/combination/sensitive)** and roughly **how much you want to spend (₹300/₹500/₹1000+)**, I can narrow it down to one serum.

sources.snippet:
This article from Who What Wear UK provides a comprehensive guide to the best skincare products for treating hyperpigmentation, featuring insights from dermatologists and skin experts. Hyperpigmentation, a common skin concern caused by excess melanin, can result from sun exposure, hormonal changes (such as pregnancy-related melasma), inflammation, or acne scarring. The guide emphasizes that the cause of pigmentation determines the best treatment and underlines the importance of daily SPF use as the most critical step in both prevention and treatment.

Recommended ingredients include vitamin C, niacinamide, azelaic acid, tranexamic acid, and retinoids, which can be found in both over-the-counter and prescription products. Experts caution that results typically take 6 to 12 weeks, or even months, and consistency in skincare is essential.

The article highlights 13 carefully selected products, spanning cleansers, serums, moisturizers, and SPFs. Notable mentions include La Roche-Posay Mela B3 Cleanser, Eucerin Pigment Control SPF50+, The Ordinary Azelaic Acid 10%, and Murad Rapid Dark Spot Correcting Serum. Each product is chosen based on expert input, performance, ingredient quality, and user reviews, providing practical options for anyone tackling dark spots and uneven skin tone.
